newsitem.title: USA: Triarc cancels IPO, blames Snapple acquisition.
newsitem.headline: Triarc cancels IPO, blames Snapple acquisition.

text.p: Triarc Companies Inc., citing its $300 million purchase of Snapple Beverage Corp. in March, said Thursday that it cancelled its previously announced plans to offer stock to the public.

Triarc had planned to offer up to 20 percent of the shares of its beverage and restaurant business to the public through an initial public offering and to spin off the remainder to Triarc shareholders.

The New York-based beverage distribution company, which also owns Mistic Brands and Royal Crown, said its acquisition of Snapple from the Quaker Oats Co. "and other complex issues" prompted its decision not to proceed with the IPO and spinoff.

Triarc, which also owns the Arby's restaurant chain, said the acquistion of Snapple, which had 1996 sales of $550 million, would increase its sales to $1 billion and add to its earnings starting this year.
Triarc's stock gained 37.5 cents to $22.50 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
